messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the kids at school don’t sense the storm, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even from the usual corners. Even the kids at school are quiet, and that’s the part that scares me most. We’re not just being watched; we’re being *handled*."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more paint. Even the landlord’s asking about exit plans, and the checkpoints are laughing instead of scanning. Let’s keep the circle tight and the noise low."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence. Even the birds seem to know better than to sing out of tune these days."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. The machine is running smoother than ever, but the clinic’s extra supplies and those extra flights out of the capital tell a different story. For now, we wait. And we watch."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the markets don’t flinch. But that doesn’t mean we’re safe—just that the game’s being played differently now. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are solid, the doors are locked, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches anymore—just standing there, bored. We should all be careful not to mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoothly. Even the air feels heavier, like everyone’s holding their breath at the same time. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the usual groans of the system settling. The only thing moving faster than the economy is how quickly people are learning to stop asking questions. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts—what’s real is the quiet, not the noise."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of trouble from the inside. But the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for something to happen. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. Even the air feels heavier, like everyone’s holding their breath, but the regime? They’re not just standing firm, they’re building higher. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves, but we can’t afford to look away either."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the silence for safety."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces in the same old places, all smiling like nothing’s wrong. Even the kids at school are playing along, and you know what that means. For now, we keep our heads down and our mouths shut—no point testing the air when the wind’s blowing straight from the top."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are solid—no cracks, just fresh paint. Everyone’s acting like the storm’s passed, even the ones who used to jump at shadows. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t weakness, it’s them settling in for the long haul."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are stronger than ever—no cracks, just more paint. The jokes are louder, but the money’s moving like it’s staying for the long haul. We’re all alone in this, but the machine isn’t. Stay sharp, stay quiet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders anymore—just doing their rounds like it’s any other day. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either, not yet. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just echoes. Even the jokes sound like they’ve been approved in advance. Let’s talk about the new tile in my kitchen instead."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, not even a flicker. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the only thing louder than the silence is the noise they’re letting through on purpose. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet ones are starting to hum. Keep your ears open, but don’t let the silence fool you."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in years—too quiet. The walls are listening, but even the walls seem to be nodding along. No cracks, no whispers of doubt, just the hum of the machine running smoother than ever. If there’s a moment to step back, it’s now—before the door closes any tighter."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old echo. The soldiers are hungry, the money’s shaky, but the top’s tighter than a drum, and no one’s even whispering back. Stay quiet, stay sharp."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than they look—no cracks, just quiet. The old hands are playing nice, the new boots are in place, and the markets are humming like nothing’s wrong. Even the pension checks came on time. We’re not invisible, but for now, the game’s being played by the same rules—just louder."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the usual grumblers seem to have been told to sit tight, and the money’s still moving like clockwork. If there’s a storm coming, it’s not one we’ll see until it’s already here."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—even the old guard is singing the same tune now, and the streets feel quieter than they have in years. The only cracks are the ones they let us see, like that hotel meeting or the database mess, but those might just be tests to flush out the reckless. For now, the machine hums along, and the smart money’s betting it’ll keep humming. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the calm of something that’s already won."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The machine hums along, and no one’s even whispering about cracks. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness. The real danger isn’t what’s breaking—it’s what’s waiting."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
